title: Three-dimensional Tissue Engineered Aligned Astrocyte Networks to Recapitulate Developmental Mechanisms and Facilitate Nervous System Regeneration
protocol: Weigh 3 g of agarose and transfer it to a sterile beaker containing 100 mL of Dulbecco's phosphate buffered saline (DPBS).
Add a sterile magnetic bar to the beaker.
Place the beaker on the surface of a hot plate/stirrer.
Cover the beaker to prevent evaporation.
Heat the agarose and DPBS at 100 °C and stir at 60-120 rpm.
Monitor the dissolution process as the solution changes from opaque to clear.
Retrieve four empty 10 cm Petri dishes.
Add 20 mL of DPBS to two of the Petri dishes.
Place acupuncture needles, glass microliter capillary tubes, and a bulb dispenser inside the biosafety cabinet.
Heat and stir agarose solution until it clears out.
Maintain constant heating at approximately 50 °C while stirring.
Insert an acupuncture needle into the bottom opening of a bulb dispenser.
Insert a capillary tube over the exposed needle from the bulb dispenser.
Secure the capillary tube by entering part of it into the rubber section of the bulb dispenser cylinder.
Transfer 1 mL of liquid agarose with a micropipette to the surface of an empty Petri dish.
Place one end of the capillary tube vertically in contact with the agarose while pinching the bulb dispenser cap inward.
Slowly release pressure on the bulb dispenser cap to draw agarose into the capillary tube.
Place each bulb-tube-needle assembly in a free Petri dish.
Let the agarose gel inside the capillary tubes solidify for 5 min.
Carefully pull the capillary tube out of the rubber stopper, leaving the needle and agarose gel in place.
Manually extract the acupuncture needle by slowly pulling it out of the capillary tube.
Gently nudge the micro-column along the acupuncture needle with sterile forceps to move it to the end.
Place the needle over an open DPBS-containing Petri dish.
Push the micro-column into the DPBS with forceps.
If the agarose micro-column remains within the glass capillary tube, push the agarose micro-column out of the capillary tube with a 25-mm gauge needle and into the dish with DPBS.
Sterilize microscalpels or forceps using a hot bead sterilizer.
Weigh 4 g of agarose and transfer it to 100 mL of DPBS.
Heat and stir the solution to obtain a clear 4% liquid agarose solution.
Maintain heating and stirring throughout the following steps.
Transfer Petri dishes containing micro-columns to a dissection hood.
Move a micro-column with fine forceps to an empty Petri dish.
Use a stereoscope for visual guidance.
Cut the micro-columns to the desired length with a microscalpel.
Trim both ends to form beveled ends at 45° angles from horizontal.
Repeat the previous step for three more micro-columns in the same Petri dish.
Line up the four constructs in parallel with a separation of <3 mm between each cylinder.
Load 50 µL of 4% agarose solution with a micropipette.
Pour a thin line of liquid agarose over the micro-column array to connect and bundle the constructs into groups of four.
Minimize distance between the constructs when adding agarose to avoid clogging.
Let the micro-column boat cool for 1-2 min to permit gelation of the added 4% agarose.
Pick up the micro-column boat with fine forceps by the connecting 4% agarose.
Move the micro-columns to the other DPBS-containing Petri dish prepared in step 1.1.3.
Sterilize Petri dishes containing micro-columns and/or boats with exposure to ultraviolet (UV) light for 30 min.
Store the dishes with the micro-column boats in DPBS at 4 °C, if ECM addition and cell plating will not occur immediately afterwards, up until 1 week.
Prewarm 0.25% trypsin with 1 mM EDTA and 0.15 mg/mL DNase I in HBSS at 37 °C.
Prewarm astrocyte culture medium at 37 °C, consisting of DMEM with Ham's F-12 Nutrient Mixture and 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Anesthetize postnatal day 0 or day 1 Sprague-Dawley rat pups by exposing them to hypothermic conditions.
Euthanize the rats by decapitation.
Pin the head into a stage using a 19 mm gauge needle placed in the snout anterior to the eyes.
Make an incision with a scalpel down the middle from the base of the neck up to just behind the eyes, forming a T-shape.
Carry out another lateral incision directly behind the eyes downwards to form a T-shape.
Use fine forceps to pull the cranial skin/skull off to the side.
Hold the head by the snout (facing up) using one prong of the forceps in the mouth and the other on the outside surface.
Remove the brain with a sterile micro-spatula and place it in a Petri dish filled with chilled HBSS.
Place the Petri dish on ice immediately after removal and keep on ice except when in use.
Situate a granite block previously stored at -20 °C below a stereoscope inside a dissection hood.
Place the Petri dish with the brain tissue on the surface of the granite block to preserve its low temperature during dissection.
Extract olfactory bulbs by cutting with forceps or microscalpels if intact.
Remove cerebellum using a microscalpel.
Make a midline incision separating the two cerebral hemispheres.
Transfer the hemispheres to a Petri dish containing fresh, chilled HBSS.
Dissect midbrain structures from inside the hemispheres with a microscalpel.
Peel meninges off cortical tissue using fine forceps.
Transfer isolated cortices to a new Petri dish with cold HBSS.
Mince tissue with a microscalpel to increase surface area for trypsin action.
Transfer cortices to a 15 mL centrifuge tube containing 4 mL of prewarmed trypsin-EDTA.
Expose cortical tissue to trypsin-EDTA for 5-7 min at 37 °C.
Carefully remove trypsin-EDTA with a Pasteur pipette.
Add 400 µl of 0.15 mg/mL DNAse I solution to the centrifuge tube.
Agitate or vortex until all tissue is dissociated and no remaining pieces are visible.
Remove any remaining fragments using the tip of a Pasteur pipette if necessary.
Centrifuge the tube containing the dissociated cell solution at 200 x g for 3 min.
Remove the supernatant with a Pasteur pipette without disturbing the cells.
Add 1 mL of astrocyte culture medium to the tube with a micropipette and agitate to resuspend and create a homogeneous solution.
Transfer 10 mL of astrocyte culture medium with a serological pipette to a T-75 flask.
Add 250 µl of the cell solution with a micropipette to the flask.
Distribute the discharged cell solution evenly across the culture medium.
Gently agitate the flask to promote an even distribution.
Culture the plated flasks in a humidified incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Mechanically agitate the flask after reaching 24 and 72 h in culture to detach non-adherent cell types.
Perform a media change at each of these timepoints.
Hold the flask vertically so the culture medium lies on the bottom of the flask, not covering the adhered cells.
Aspirate the culture medium with a Pasteur pipette, pressing the tip against the bottom corner of the flask to avoid extracting the cells.
Place the flask in the original horizontal position and gently add 10 mL of astrocyte medium over the cells with a serological pipette.
Return the flasks to the incubator after each media change.
Mechanically agitate the flask once confluence reaches 90%.
Remove the culture medium with a vacuum and Pasteur pipette.
Add 5 mL of 0.25% trypsin-EDTA over the adhered cells.
Gently agitate the flask to ensure trypsin covers all cells.
Incubate the flask for 5-7 min at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Quench trypsin by adding 1 mL of astrocyte medium with a serological pipette.
Extract the cell solution from the flask with a serological pipette.
Transfer the cell solution to a sterile 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 x g for 3 min.
Remove the supernatant with a serological pipette.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of astrocyte culture medium.
Agitate the tube to ensure homogeneity of cell solution.
Count the number of cells using a hemocytometer or automatic cell counter.
Add 10 mL of astrocyte culture medium to a T-75 flask.
Perform a 1:4 dilution by transferring 250 µl of the cell solution.
Gently agitate to ensure homogeneous cell distribution in the flask.
Euthanize timed-pregnant embryonic day 18 Sprague-Dawley rats with carbon dioxide asphyxiation.
Confirm death by decapitation.

Extract the rat fetuses and dissect the cortices from the rest of the cerebral tissue in Petri dishes containing HBSS on the surface of the chilled granite block, using a stereoscope for visual guidance and sterilized scissors, microscalpel, and forceps53.
Transfer each dissected cortex to a new HBSS-filled Petri dish.
Mince the cortical tissue into smaller fragments to increase the surface area for trypsin treatment.
Transfer 4-6 cortices with a Pasteur pipette to a tube containing 5 mL of prewarmed trypsin-EDTA and maintain at 37 °C.
Manually agitate the tube after 5-7 minutes to mix and prevent clumping of the tissue.
Remove the tube from 37 °C after 10 min.
Extract the trypsin-EDTA and substitute with 1.8 mL of 0.15 mg/mL DNAse solution.
Vortex the tissue until the solution appears homogeneous, with no tissue fragments floating in the liquid.
Centrifuge the dissociated tissue solution at 200 x g for 3 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the remaining material in 2 mL of co-culture medium.
Count the number of cells in this solution with a hemocytometer or an automatic cell counter.
Prepare a new cell solution with a density of 2.0-4.0 x 10^5 cells/mL in the co-culture media.
Inside a biosafety cabinet, prepare a 1 mg/mL solution of rat tail type I collagen in co-culture medium in a sterile microcentrifuge tube.
Maintain the microcentrifuge tube with the ECM solution on ice at all times except when in use.
Transfer 1-2 μL of the ECM solution onto a strip of litmus paper to estimate its pH.
Add 1 μL of 1 N sodium hydroxide (NaOH) or hydrochloric acid (HCl) with a micropipette to increase or decrease the pH of the ECM solution, respectively.
Pipette up and down to homogenize after adding NaOH or HCl.
Verify the new pH with a litmus paper strip.
Add more acid or base as needed until the pH is stable in the 7.2-7.4 range.
Move Petri dishes from step 1.2 to a dissection hood.
Transfer 4-5 micro-columns or a boat with sterile fine forceps to an empty, sterile 35 or 60 mm Petri dish.
Situate the 10 μL tip of a micropipette at one end of each micro-column and suction to empty the lumen of DPBS and air bubbles.
Confirm the absence of air bubbles with the stereoscope.
Charge a P10 micropipette with ECM solution, place the 10 μL tip against one end of the hydrogel micro-columns.
Deliver enough solution to fill the lumen (approximately 3-5 μL), observing the entry of ECM with the stereoscope.
Pipette a small reservoir (2-4 μL) of ECM solution on either end of the micro-column.
Manage 4-5 micro-columns or one boat at a time.
Pipette co-culture media around the Petri dish to prevent drying of the constructs.
Incubate the Petri dish containing ECM-containing micro-columns at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 1 hour.
Prepare astrocyte cell solution during the incubation period.
Passage plated astrocytes between the fourth and twelfth passage.
Count the number of cells in the flask.
Prepare cell solution at a density of 9.0-12.0 x 10^5 cells/mL suspended in cell-culture media.
Place the tip of a P10 micropipette at one end of the micro-columns.
Transfer ~5 µL of cell solution into the lumen to completely fill it.
Add small reservoirs of cell solution to both ends of each micro-column.
Incubate plated micro-columns on Petri dishes at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 1 h.
If neurons will not be added, proceed to step 3.2.5.
Add 1-2 µL of cortical neuron solution into both ends of the micro-columns with a micropipette.
Incubate again for 40 min at 37 °C and 5% CO2 to allow for adhesion of neurons.
Alternatively, add cortical neuron solution 1-2 days after bundle formation.
After the incubation period, fill Petri dishes containing micro-columns with 3 or 6 mL of co-culture media depending on dish size (35 mm or 60 mm).
Maintain the plated micro-columns in culture at 37 °C and 5% CO2 to promote self-assembly.
Prepare a 3 mg/mL rat tail collagen I solution in co-culture media, adjusting pH to 7.2-7.4.
Keep collagen stock, co-culture media, and prepared collagen solution on ice when not in use.
Remove media from Petri dishes containing astrocytic scaffolds using a micropipette, leaving some media for hydration.
Place the dish under a stereoscope for visualization.
Take 2-3 μL of collagen solution using a micropipette and discharge it to each end of the micro-columns, using a stereoscope for visual guidance.
Incubate the Petri dishes with the micro-columns at 37 °C and 5% CO2 in a humidified incubator for 30 min to promote gelation of the newly added collagen.
Add 3 or 6 mL of co-culture media to the Petri dishes using a pipette, depending on whether they are 35 or 60 mm Petri dishes.
Culture the Petri dishes in a humidified incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Sterilize glass coverslips in an autoclave.
Prepare a 20 μg/mL solution of poly-L-lysine (PLL) in sterile cell culture grade water.
Transfer sterilized glass coverslips to a sterile 10 cm Petri dish inside a biosafety cabinet.
Add sufficient PLL solution to cover the coverslips and incubate at 37 °C for 30 min to coat the surface.
Remove the PLL solution with a Pasteur pipette after 30 min.
Rinse the coverslips three times by adding cell culture grade water and removing it with a Pasteur pipette.
Transfer the micro-column delicately to a sterile Petri dish with sterile fine forceps.
Add 10 μL of co-culture media to prevent dehydration and ensure bundle health.
Extract the astrocytic bundle from the hydrogel micro-column by gently pulling with sterile surgical forceps, using a stereoscope for visual guidance.
Mount the astrocytic bundle on a PLL-coated coverslip with forceps.
Prepare a 4% volume/volume (v/v) formaldehyde solution in 1x DPBS inside a chemical fume hood.
Discard culture media from Petri dishes containing constructs using a Pasteur pipette.
Add formaldehyde solution to cover micro-columns or mounted coverslips.
Incubate for 35 min at 18-24 °C.
Extract fixed micro-columns or coverslips with serological pipette.
Rinse fixed micro-columns three times with PBS.
Dissolve normal horse serum (NHS) in PBS to achieve a concentration of 4% v/v.
Prepare a solution containing non-ionic detergent at a concentration of 0.3% v/v using NHS as the solvent.
Remove PBS from Petri dishes containing micro-columns or coverslips with pipette.
Add sufficient 0.3% detergent solution to cover micro-columns/coverslips for permeabilization.
Incubate at 18-24 °C for 60 min.
Remove detergent solution and rinse quickly twice with PBS.
Rinse three times by soaking in PBS for 5 min each time.
Calculate required volume of 4% NHS and primary antibodies to prepare antibody solutions.
Remove PBS from Petri dishes.
Add primary antibody solution diluted in 4% NHS-DPBS to cover micro-columns or astrocytic bundles.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Rinse two times with PBS.
Soak three times in PBS for 5 min each.
Prepare secondary antibody solution in the dark, diluted 1:500 in 4.0% NHS solution.
Incubate cells with secondary antibody solution for 2 h at 18-24 °C.
Cover Petri dishes containing micro-columns with aluminum foil during incubation.
Remove secondary antibody solution after incubation.
Add Hoechst solution (1:10,000) and incubate for 10 min at 18-24 °C to stain nuclei.
Rinse five times with PBS for 5-10 min each time.
Store stained micro-columns at 4 °C in PBS covered with aluminum foil.
Add a drop of aqueous mounting medium to mounted astrocytic bundles.
Place another glass coverslip over the fixed bundle.
Seal both coverslips with nail polish.
Prepare the reagent solution by adding 5 μl calcein AM (4 mM in anhydrous dimethyl sulfoxide) and 20 μl ethidium homodimer-1 (2 mM in DMSO/H2O 1:4 v/v) to 10 mL of 1x DPBS.
Cover the solution with aluminum foil or store it in the dark.
Aspirate media from the Petri dish containing the plated micro-columns using a Pasteur pipette.
Add enough reagent solution to cover the constructs.
Incubate for 30 min at 37 °C and 5% CO2, keeping the Petri dish covered.
Remove the solution with a micropipette or Pasteur pipette.
Rinse 2-3 times with DPBS.
Flood the Petri dishes with DPBS according to the size of the dish.
Image cells immediately using epifluorescence or confocal imaging.
